$comment: D-HIR-BRACE-INIT-LOWERING-RECURSES-PER-BRACE-LEVEL-AND-A-CAP-IS-UNAVAILABLE end-to-end witness: `lowerBraceInit` <-> `lowerExprOrBraceInit` (src/hir/lowering/cst_to_hir.cpp) used to call each other once per `{`, two host frames per brace level, and they are now ONE explicit heap level stack (`BraceLevel`), with the union arm folded in as a one-slot level instead of kept as a second recursion edge. The program is `struct S256 g = {{{ ... {42} ... }}};` over 256 nested `struct Sk { struct S(k-1) a; int pad; };`: every level's `.a` takes the next brace level and every level's `.pad` is OMITTED, so one file drives the 256-level brace DESCENT and the per-level ZERO-FILL (flattenInitSlot + synthZeroOrError) together. main checks the value at the bottom (42), the zero-fill at the OUTERMOST level (g.pad) and the zero-fill at the INNERMOST one, then returns 42 -- so a lowering that dropped a level, mis-ordered the slots, or left a pad uninitialized returns 1/2/3 instead of 42. Both references agree on this program at -O0 and -O2 (MEASURED: gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 both build and run it, exit 42).
$commentWhatThisDoesNotWitness: HONEST, and it is the reason 256 is not larger. This example CANNOT witness the CEILING the conversion moved, only the OUTPUT the conversion had to preserve. The unit pin (tests/hir/test_frontend_deep_nesting_costs_heap.cpp, `NestedBraceInitializerCostsHeap` at 8192) is where the ceiling lives, because it runs on the ORDINARY ~1 MiB thread; the CLI builds every CU inside substrate::callOnLargeStack(64 MiB) and its ceiling for this shape is set by a LATER tier: MEASURED through `dsscp --compile` on this leg, 1000 builds and runs and 1100 dies 0xC00000FD -- the SAME pair before and after this conversion, so no corpus depth exists that is green after and red before. 256 is chosen instead as the deepest bracket nesting ALL THREE references accept (clang refuses at 257 with `bracket nesting level exceeded maximum of 256`), which puts it squarely inside the union on every leg with ~4x margin under the tightest measured wall -- a deep example that flakes on the leg with the fattest frames would be worse than no example.

optimizedPipelines.$comment: The release arm proves the 256-level aggregate the front end just built survives the full optimizer pipeline and still exits 42 -- a pass that mishandled a deep ConstructAggregate would show up here and nowhere else in this example. `mustDifferFromBaseline` is MEASURED, not assumed: on x86_64:pe64-x86_64-windows-exec the runner reported `optimized-arms-ran=1 compared=1 byte-identical=0`, so the pipeline really does rewrite this program (the 768 loads of the deep member chain collapse) rather than passing it through. ⚠ The release arm also emits `warning[X_OptFixpointTruncated]` on this input -- the root fixpoint node stops at its cap of 1 iteration with 2 passes still mutating -- so the optimized image here is CORRECT but is not the program a converged pipeline would emit. That is the optimizer's cap, not this example's, and it is reported rather than papered over.
